macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. inflation cooled in July, easing pressure on the Fed
items.summary: The Labor Department said July inflation fell to 3.4% year over year, with core CPI also slowing, which reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep rates steady near term. Markets shifted to price in lower odds of a September rate hike after the report.

items.title: U.S. stocks closed higher as CoreWeave earnings boosted AI sentiment
items.summary: The S&P 500 finished higher on Wednesday, led by gains in AI-related names after CoreWeave reported strong results and lifted its outlook. Chipmakers and data center operators also advanced on the improved forecast backdrop.

items.title: Fed policy bets ease after softer CPI and weak labor data
items.summary: Traders reduced the probability of a near-term Federal Reserve rate hike after the benign July inflation reading and a prior weak jobs report. Fed funds futures now imply lower odds of a September hike than a week ago.

items.title: Dollar stalls and U.S. yields hold after inflation data
items.summary: The dollar index was flat to slightly lower after the July CPI report, while Treasury yields were little changed. The move reflected expectations that the Fed is less likely to tighten policy soon.

items.title: Asian markets mixed as investors digest U.S. inflation and AI-led risk appetite
items.summary: Asian shares were mixed, with traders balancing softer U.S. inflation and expectations for stable Fed policy against lingering caution in global markets. Japan’s market also drew attention after major currency intervention efforts to support the yen.

items.title: Japan intervenes in currency markets to support the yen
items.summary: Japan reportedly carried out a record-sized yen-buying intervention, with authorities said to have deployed nearly $40 billion amid sharp yen weakness. The move underscored continued pressure on the currency and heightened policy attention in Tokyo.

items.title: Oil prices slipped overnight as traders weighed macro data
items.summary: Overnight trade saw both major oil benchmarks ease, with U.S. crude and Brent lower. The move came as investors focused on inflation data, rate expectations, and broader risk sentiment.

items.title: India’s rupee held up after RBI intervention
items.summary: The rupee ended modestly higher as Reserve Bank of India dollar sales helped stabilize trading despite pressure from higher crude prices. The currency traded in a narrow band during the session.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major crypto prices were broadly mixed, with BTC holding near $63K-$64K and ETH around $1.9K
items.summary: Across the latest market updates, Bitcoin traded around $63,400-$64,000 and Ethereum hovered near $1,875-$1,900, while XRP, Solana, and Dogecoin were also slightly lower on the day. Several reports tied the move to a cooler-than-expected U.S. CPI print and continuing ETF flow dynamics.[5][12][14][18]

items.title: Crypto market steadies after inflation data as Bitcoin briefly revisits $64K
items.summary: Market commentary said the July U.S. inflation reading matched expectations and helped limit downside, with Bitcoin trading between roughly $63,185 and $64,381 in the session. One report said spot Bitcoin ETF inflows helped cushion losses even as total crypto market capitalization slipped modestly.[14][19]

items.title: Regulatory spotlight: Hawaii approves crypto ATM ban, with rule taking effect October 1
items.summary: Hawaii’s crypto ATM ban was one of the clearest regulatory developments in the latest news flow, with the rule set to take effect on Oct. 1. Related U.S. state-level enforcement news also noted Arizona refunds to scam victims tied to crypto ATM cases.[3][6]

items.title: U.S.-UK crypto pact signals direction rather than binding rules
items.summary: A reported U.S.-UK crypto pact was described as setting direction for future cooperation but not creating binding rules yet. The same coverage framed it as an important policy signal rather than a finalized regulatory framework.[6]

items.title: Russia’s central bank proposed regulated trading for Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT
items.summary: One of the most notable global policy stories was a report that the Central Bank of Russia proposed allowing Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT to trade on regulated platforms. If implemented, that would represent a meaningful expansion of legally supervised crypto access in Russia.[12]

items.title: Goldman Sachs move toward NEOS acquisition could expand Bitcoin-linked ETF exposure
items.summary: Crypto market coverage highlighted Goldman Sachs planning to acquire ETF manager NEOS for up to $2.25 billion, gaining a Bitcoin options income ETF with about $1 billion in assets. The deal was presented as a notable TradFi-crypto crossover development rather than a pure on-chain event.[3][10]

items.title: Project and infrastructure news: BTCPay Server warned of an actively exploited critical vulnerability
items.summary: BTCPay Server issued an emergency security advisory saying versions prior to 2.4.2 contain a critical vulnerability that has been actively exploited, with user funds reported stolen. This was one of the most consequential project-level security stories in the latest feed.[10]

items.title: Market rotation news: GSR reportedly raised Solana exposure and cut Bitcoin exposure
items.summary: A portfolio-allocation report said GSR increased Solana to 43.6% while reducing Bitcoin to 16.9%, suggesting continued institutional rotation within crypto exposures. The item did not provide full methodology, so it should be treated as directional market intelligence.[6]
